meta.title: Inventory and allocation analyst at a multi-location resort retailer
meta.industry: Resort retail, six shops across two resorts
meta.blurb: Decides how stock moves between the warehouse and the shops, and keeps counts accurate.

opportunities.quote: I combine their NetSuite on-hand and sales in Excel for the Monday report
opportunities.why: You pull NetSuite on-hand and sales for several shops and combine them in Excel for the weekly report.

habits.name: Grouping similar tasks
becauseTasks: Excel: Plan transfers between shops, Build the weekly replenishment report, Reconcile shop counts with the system, Month-end inventory valuation
habits.firstStep: Put the tasks that use the same tool into one block on your calendar.

transcript.question: How many shops do you check stock levels for in "Check stock levels by shop"?
transcript.answer: Six shops. I combine their NetSuite on-hand and sales in Excel for the Monday report.

transcript.question: Who receives the Monday report from "Check stock levels by shop"?
transcript.answer: Buyer and store operations, via email on Mondays.

transcript.question: For "Build the weekly replenishment report", where does the data come from, and who receives the finished report?
options: Stock report from t1, sent to store ops
Shop emails, sent to buyer and ops
Mixed sources, shared on a drive
transcript.answer: NetSuite on-hand export plus point-of-sale sales, combined in Excel; emailed to the buyer and store operations.

transcript.question: For "Plan transfers between shops", where does the information come from, and who gets the finished plan?
options: From my replenishment report; sent to store operations
From NetSuite stock data; sent to shop managers
From shop requests by email; sent to the buyer
From the Monday report; entered into NetSuite
